text: Imagine looking up… and every night, the Moon is a little bigger.
No impact. No explosion. It just keeps creeping closer, night after night.
Right now, the Moon is about three hundred and eighty-four thousand kilometres away.
You cannot feel its pull. But the oceans can. Twice a day, it lifts them into the tides.
And tidal pull follows a frightening rule: halve the distance, and it becomes eight times stronger.
The Moon looks almost twice as wide. And the tides are about seven times stronger.
High tide no longer stops at the quay.
Now the pull on the oceans is more than fifty times stronger than today.
With every high tide, the sea pours into the harbour…
…and when it pulls back, it leaves the ships behind, stranded in the streets.
But water is not the only thing the Moon can pull on.
